title: ICMPv6 computed-zero checksum convention diverges: C reconstructs 0xFFFF, Python/Rust keep 0x0000
description: P3, found during project-LICHEN-worker6-5b1y (the UDP sibling of this divergence). C icmpv6_checksum (lichen/subsys/lichen/schc/schc_checksum.c:100-106) routes through finalize_checksum which maps computed-zero to 0xFFFF (schc_checksum.c:53-63); Python icmpv6_checksum (python/src/lichen/ipv6/icmpv6.py:79-88) and Rust icmpv6_checksum_parts (rust/lichen-schc/src/codec.rs:650-655) and Rust headers.rs icmpv6_checksum return the raw complement, keeping 0x0000. For ICMPv6 a zero checksum is legal (the RFC 8200 8.1 zero-prohibition is UDP-specific), and BOTH wire values verify as valid when the true checksum is zero (one-complement: 0x0000 and 0xFFFF are equivalent in the validity sum), so there is no rejection asymmetry - but the reconstructed byte streams differ: a rule-2 (ICMPv6 echo) round trip of a packet whose true checksum computes to zero reproduces 0x0000 in Python/Rust and 0xFFFF in C, failing byte-identical round-trip assertions and the shared-vector discipline for that (statistically rare) packet class. Probability per distinct packet ~1/65536, and no existing corpus row hits it (checked: icmpv6 echo vectors have nonzero computed checksums). Fix needs a coordinated convention decision (C scopes the mapping to UDP like Python/Rust, or Python+Rust adopt 0xFFFF for ICMPv6 - RFC is silent; pick one and align all three), then pin with a shared rule-2 vector whose ICMPv6 checksum computes to zero. Do NOT scope-creep 5b1y's UDP fix: that one is protocol-correct as-is.
